title: Night Gallery in Hollywood
summary: He scored Night Gallery for a season and a half.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: I went to the coast in '71 to do 1776 and ran into the chap I was talking about earlier at MCA. He said come on, he showed me the place, they gave me the grand tour and in the process I met a guy with whom I had written three musicals, of which "10,000 B.C." is one, and some other things we have in there.
None of them came off as
musical, but he drifted to the coast and became a producer, director out there, and it was his show, it had to be "Night Gallery", so I did that and that was good.
How many episodes did you do?
I did a season and a half, until it went off the air.
That was the early seventies, or something like that?
I started the middle of '71 and it took us through '72 when I stopped.

Every once in a while he calls me out to do something, but that's the only guy I know. I liked that but I didn't feel it was strong enough to move out to the coast and take my chances, because there's no reason to think that I would be any more commercially viable than I was here.
So I wait now for the telephone to ring.
They know where to find you.
